chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza al-Bata'ini, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever performs the witr prayer reciting the mu'awwadhatayn and 'Say: He is God, the One,' it is said to him: 'O servant of God, be glad, for God has accepted your witr.'

key_terms.المعوذتين: The two protective surahs (al-Falaq 113 and al-Nas 114)
key_terms.قل هو الله أحد: Surah al-Ikhlas (112), the chapter of Divine Unity
key_terms.وتر: The witr prayer, an odd-numbered supererogatory prayer performed at night

ai.seo_question: What surahs should be recited in the witr prayer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) encourages reciting Surahs al-Falaq (113), al-Nas (114), and al-Ikhlas (112) during the witr prayer. The witr is a supererogatory prayer performed after the night prayer, and the narration promises divine acceptance for one who recites these three surahs therein.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
